name: Gamepad presence
plain: Lists connected game controllers, but only after a button press on the controller.
meaning: Reveals a controller is plugged in or paired (id string includes vendor and product IDs). Hidden until the user presses a button, so it is not a silent probe.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: id
fields.range: e.g. Xbox 360 Controller (STANDARD GAMEPAD Vendor: 045e Product: 028e)

limits.headline: Can see a game controller only after you press a button on it
limits.user_action: You press a button on a connected controller while the page is open
can: List connected controllers, including maker and product codes
Use the controller to play a game in the page
Tell when a controller connects or disconnects
cannot: See a controller before you press a button on it
See controllers when the tab is in the background
Silently check; pressing a button is required

story.what_it_is: Lists game controllers connected to your device, but only after you press a button on one.

marketing.name: Gamepad API
marketing.pitch: Documents how pages read controllers so web games can feel like console games.

story.for_you: You plug in or pair a controller, then press a button. Only then the page can see it. Nothing shows up before that, so it is not a silent check.
story.for_makers: Games and cloud gaming sites want controller support to feel like a console. The press-a-button rule stops sites from quietly listing devices. The controller name still shows the brand, which is a small fingerprint clue.

use_cases.example: A cloud gaming site such as Xbox Cloud Gaming shows controller buttons on screen after you press a button on your Xbox pad.
A browser platformer or racing game switches from keyboard hints to PlayStation button icons when it sees a DualSense.
A multiplayer party game in the browser assigns player 1 to 4 as each friend presses a button on their pad.
A web game supports an adaptive controller so players with limited mobility can join in.
A browser media center app lets you browse shows with a gamepad on a living room TV.
A web robotics simulator lets students drive a virtual robot with a joystick.
A fingerprinting script records the controller ID string once a user presses a button.

risks: Brand and model of controller revealed

technical_bounds: Needs user input on the pad first
Only while the page is focused

history.change: Secure context and focused-page needed; Permissions-Policy gamepad added
